feature1.prompt: The query optimization in YearLookup currently breaks filtering by "__iso_year" because the backend operations do not differentiate between standard year boundaries and ISO-8601 week‐numbering year boundaries. The fix requires modifying the low-level methods that compute the year lookup bounds for date and datetime fields so that when an ISO year is requested the functions compute the correct lower and upper boundaries using ISO-8601 rules. This means adding an extra parameter to these methods and introducing logic to calculate the boundaries through ISO-specific date construction. After the fix, when the iso_year flag is active, the backend will return the appropriate boundaries and avoid returning incorrect data for filters that rely on ISO week-numbering.
feature1.hint_texts: Update the methods in django/db/backends/base/operations.py to support a new 'iso_year' parameter. When iso_year is true, use ISO-8601 functions (such as fromisocalendar) to determine the first and last date/time of the ISO year rather than using the simple January 1 and December 31 boundaries. Ensure that both date and datetime fields are handled correctly and that timezone awareness is preserved when needed.
feature1.entrypoint: File: django/db/backends/base/operations.py. Functions: year_lookup_bounds_for_date_field and year_lookup_bounds_for_datetime_field. Start by locating the existing functions (around line 526) and add the iso_year parameter along with conditional logic to compute ISO-8601 boundaries.

feature2.prompt: Filtering by "__iso_year" in YearLookup currently returns wrong data due to the way the optimization applies a BETWEEN operator even when an ISO-8601 based annotation is expected. The issue is that the YearLookup integration does not pass along the necessary information for ISO-8601 week-numbering years, resulting in the backend using standard year boundaries. The fix involves updating the YearLookup class so that it detects when an ISO year is in use and then calls the backend operations using the iso_year flag. Once corrected, filters that use "__iso_year" will correctly translate into SQL queries based on ISO-8601 year boundaries and return accurate results.
feature2.hint_texts: Modify the YearLookup class in django/db/models/lookups.py to inspect the lookup expression. Import or check for the ExtractIsoYear instance and set the iso_year flag accordingly when calling the backend's year lookup bound functions. Review how the iso_year parameter is passed in order to ensure that the SQL query uses the correct BETWEEN boundaries. This integration must fully leverage the API exposed by the backend operations modifications.
feature2.entrypoint: File: django/db/models/lookups.py. Class: YearLookup, specifically its year_lookup_bounds method and any related SQL generation in as_sql. Begin by ensuring that the lookup correctly determines whether to use ISO-8601 boundaries based on the type of the lookup expression.

Feature2 must consume this API by passing the flag appropriately in the YearLookup class. Both features rely on consistent handling of ISO-8601 week-numbering logic in the backend operations.
collaboration_points.communication_needs: Developers working on Feature2 should communicate with those implementing Feature1 to ensure that the new parameter and boundary calculations are correctly integrated. Both teams must coordinate on test changes and verify that any modifications in method signatures or expected behavior are reflected in the YearLookup integration.
